pairs: I am a flower of the open field and a lily of the steep valleys.
Groom: Like a lily among the thorns,
so is my loved one among the daughters.
Bride to Chorus: Like an apple tree among the trees of the forest,
so is my beloved among the sons.
Sub umbra illius quem desideraveram sedi,
I sat beneath the shadow of the one whom I desired,
et fructus ejus dulcis gutturi meo.
and his fruit was sweet to my palate.
He brought me into the storeroom of wine.
He set charity in order within me.
His left hand is under my head,
and his right hand shall embrace me.
by the does and the stags of the open field,
not to disturb or awaken the beloved,
even for as long as she wills.
Behold, he arrives leaping along the mountains,
Similis est dilectus meus capreæ, hinnuloque cervorum. En ipse stat post parietem nostrum, respiciens per fenestras, prospiciens per cancellos.
My beloved is like a doe and like a young stag.
Lo, he stands beyond our wall,
columba mea, formosa mea, et veni:
jam enim hiems transiit; imber abiit, et recessit.
Lo, my beloved speaks to me:
vox turturis audita est in terra nostra;
ficus protulit grossos suos; vineæ florentes dederunt odorem suum. Surge, amica mea, speciosa mea, et veni:
For winter has now past; the rain has decreased and gone away.
The flowers have appeared in our land;
in caverna maceriæ, ostende mihi faciem tuam,
the time for pruning has arrived.
sonet vox tua in auribus meis: vox enim tua dulcis, et facies tua decora.
The voice of the turtledove has been heard in our land.
Capite nobis vulpes parvulas quæ demoliuntur vineas:
The fig tree has brought forth its green figs; the flowering vines bestow their odor. Rise up,
my love, my brilliant one, and advance.
My dove in the clefts of the rock, in the hollows of the wall,
Let your voice sound in my ears. For your voice is sweet, and your face is graceful.
Chorus to Groom and Bride: Capture for us the little foxes,
which are tearing down the vines; for our vineyard has flourished.
Bride to Chorus: My beloved is for me,
and I am for him. He pastures among the lilies,
until the day rises and the shadows decline.
O my beloved. Be like a doe and like a young stag upon the mountains of Bether.
